title: Sanity Signature Suite and Eval Matrix for Release Rollouts
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Goal: build a compact, fast-running "sanity signature" suite plus an extensible eval matrix that combinedly act as the preflight gate for release candidates and LTS promotions. The sanity signature must run within 10 minutes across our standard canary pool and provide deterministic correctness checks (token-level diffs where applicable), KV-cache integrity probes, and targeted microbenchmarks for P50/P95 token latency and memory regression signals. The eval matrix augments the signature with workload-targeted regression checks (chat, long-context completion, embedding throughput) and model-variant-aware thresholds.

Scope and constraints:
- Must be lightweight enough to run on the canary cluster during automated preflight without delaying rollouts (>10 minute target).
- Deterministic probes for correctness should include a small corpus of canonical prompts per model family, KV-cache warmup validations, and a fixed sampling seed for nondeterministic models.
- Perf gates are soft for lower tiers but P0 for LTS promotion: any LTS candidate exceeding configured delta thresholds (p50 > +15% or p95 > +25% vs baseline) must block promotion and open an investigation ticket.
- Provide an automated verdict (PASS/WARN/FAIL) with actionable diagnostics: failing inputs, latency histograms, trace IDs, kernel selection differences, and a suggested rollback or fallback variant.

Implementation plan:
1) Define signature corpus and canonical inputs per model family (initial commit: 20 prompts spanning chat/completion/embedding).
2) Implement KV-cache probe harness (warmup + consistency check) as a standalone binary that emits JSON lines for ingestion.
3) Add microbench module for p50/p95 token latency, memory footprint, and throughput under small synthetic batching patterns.
4) Integrate into preflight runner as a short-stage job and wire verdicts into rollout gating APIs (canary -> gradual -> LTS).
5) Build an eval matrix runner that parametrizes suites by model, sequence length, batch size, and quantization profile.
6) Dashboards and alerts: create per-release and per-model dashboards in Grafana and link to the release page; add PagerDuty playbook mappings for FAIL on LTS candidates.

Rollout and usage:
- Day 0: land corpus and KV probe; enable non-blocking (WARN) runs on nightly builds to collect baselines.
- Day 7: enable blocking for canary promotions; use run history to tune thresholds and reduce false positives.
- Day 21: LTS promotion requires green verdict.

Notes on false positives and tuning:
- We will store a 30-day baseline history and use rolling medians to avoid reacting to transient infra noise.
- Provide an "accept baseline" action for known-good regressions tied to release notes so release engineers can document trade-offs.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/Sanity+Signature+Spec (draft)
- Prototype PR (runtime harness): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5890
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/release-validation/sanity-signature
acceptance_criteria: Sanity signature corpus defined and checked into repo
KV-cache probe binary produces deterministic output and is integrated into preflight runner
Perf microbench produces p50/p95 and memory metrics and stores them in TSDB
Automated PASS/WARN/FAIL verdict emitted by preflight runner and visible in rollout UI
Dashboards and alert rules created; PagerDuty playbook documented
LTS promotion blocked on FAIL verdict and an investigation runbook exists
